title: Milei Backs Trump for US Midterms, Calls Vote Crucial for the West
excerpt: Argentina's president told a Washington gala that conservatives cannot give an inch in Latin America, repaying Trump's $20 billion swap backing a year earlier.
body:
• Argentine President Javier Milei used a Hispanic Heritage gala in Washington on Wednesday to urge a stronger showing for President Donald Trump in November's US midterm elections, calling the vote crucial for the West.
  • Milei said conservatives "cannot give an inch" in Latin America, according to AFP reporting carried by Al Jazeera.
  • The endorsement repays Trump's backing a year earlier, when a $20 billion US Treasury currency swap helped Milei's government through its own legislative elections.
  • Milei's 36-hour Washington trip also targeted investors, with a US Chamber of Commerce address and meetings with energy executives.

Argentine President Javier Milei has publicly backed his ally, US President Donald Trump, ahead of November's midterm elections, telling a Washington audience that the vote matters for the West as a whole. Milei made the appeal on Wednesday at a Hispanic Heritage gala in the US capital, where he received an award from a Hispanic association, according to Al Jazeera.

Conservatives, he said, "cannot give an inch in our reconquest of the hemisphere," according to Agence France-Presse. The language framed the US vote as part of a wider contest for Latin America, where Milei has positioned himself as the leading voice of a free-market right aligned with Washington.

"Cannot give an inch in our reconquest of the hemisphere."

— Javier Milei, President of Argentina

A debt being repaid

The endorsement follows a year of unusually direct American support for Milei. Trump backed him firmly during Argentina's own legislative elections a year ago and has called him his "favorite president." The centrepiece of that support was a $20 billion currency swap between the US Treasury and Argentina's central bank, announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in which the United States exchanged dollars for pesos shortly after Milei's party lost a key provincial election.

Trump made the conditional nature of the package explicit at the time, saying US support depended on Milei winning. Democratic lawmakers criticised the arrangement, accusing the administration of prioritising a foreign bailout while the US government was shut down, and Argentine markets wobbled when Trump warned Washington would not be "generous" if Milei lost. Analysts have argued the swap, together with Trump's endorsement, helped Milei succeed in those polls.

Business as well as politics

The Washington trip was not only political. Milei flew in on Wednesday for meetings with investors and is due to address the US Chamber of Commerce on Thursday. Coverage of the visit summarised by Particle News describes a tightly staged 36-hour schedule combining the gala, the Chamber speech — titled "The Argentine case" and introduced by Energy Secretary Chris Wright — and meetings with energy investors including Harold Hamm and Andy Kleinman to pitch Argentine hydrocarbons, including the Vaca Muerta shale formation.

That combination is the pattern of the Milei-Trump relationship: ideological alignment presented to voters, and market access pursued with investors. A stronger Republican showing in November would preserve the administration that underwrote Argentina's swap line and championed Milei's programme abroad.

What to watch

Milei's Chamber address on Thursday will show how far he ties Argentina's economic pitch to the US electoral outcome. Beyond Washington, the two governments are coordinating deeper technical and security ties, and a visit to Argentina by Vice President JD Vance is planned for mid-November, according to the Particle News summary. For now, Milei has made his preference unmistakable: the Argentine president who benefited from Trump's intervention in his own election year is returning the favour in America's.
